podcast.body: A hit song from "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" performed by the Red Hot Chili Peppers on "Saturday Night Live." John Frusciante's "woozy and weird" guitar playing and dissonant vocals during this performance were seen by Anthony Kiedis as a deliberate sabotage, leading to a significant confrontation between the two, with Kiedis suspecting Frusciante was on heroin. "But it's with the second song, the performance of Under the Bridge, that was The Final Straw."

podcast.body: The first note plucked by John Frusciante from this song was used in an experiment where it was played for half a second and also reversed. Despite being played backward and for such a brief duration, the brain's rapid and efficient musical memory retrieval allowed for correct identification of the song by listeners. "Yeah, that's a half second of John Fruciante plucking the first note of under the bridge by the red hot chili peppers."

podcast.body: This song is about lead singer Anthony Kiedis's regular spot to score heroin in downtown Los Angeles. Although Kiedis has never publicly disclosed the exact location, possible real-world inspirations include a pedestrian tunnel under Wilshire Boulevard in MacArthur Park, an underpass where the Santa Monica Freeway crosses Hoover Street, the Second Street tunnel under Grand Avenue, the First Street bridge over Figueroa, or the Myra Bridge in Silver Lake. The music video for the song was partly filmed at the Belmont Tunnel, a former subway excavation site known for drug deals. "The Chili Peppers sing about scoring heroin under some bridge, a real bridge, in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
